proposals.before: In 721, the ninth year of Kaiyuan, the Shuofang Army military commissioner was established, commanding the Chanyu Grand Protectorate, six prefectures (Xia, Salt, Sui, Yin, Feng, and Sheng), the Dingyuan and Feng'an garrisons, and the eastern, central, and western Accept-the-Surrender fortresses.
proposals.after: In 721, the ninth year of Kaiyuan, the Shuofang Army military commissioner was established, commanding the Chanyu Grand Protectorate, six prefectures (Xia, Yan, Sui, Yin, Feng, and Sheng), the Dingyuan and Feng'an garrisons, and the eastern, central, and western Accept-the-Surrender fortresses.
proposals.reason: 鹽州 is the prefecture Yan, not a common noun Salt; the idiomatic list should keep the toponym.

proposals.after: In 728, the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, the Dahun Protectorate was abolished.

proposals.after: The Shanxi West observation commissioner gained the chief defense commissioner in its duties.

proposals.before: The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was reinstated, filled concurrently by the Left Censorate vice censor-in-chief at Luoyang; Ru Prefecture was restored to his command and the Shanxi West defense and observation commissioner was abolished.
proposals.after: The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was reinstated, filled concurrently by the vice censor-in-chief of the detached Censorate at the eastern capital; Ru Prefecture was restored to his command and the Shanxi West defense and observation commissioner was abolished.
proposals.reason: 留臺 is the detached eastern-capital Censorate, not the Left Censorate (左臺); Luoyang is not in the Chinese of this unit.

proposals.before: The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was restored; the Left Censorate vice censor-in-chief at the eastern capital held the post concurrently; it again held Ru Prefecture; the Shanxi West defense and observation commissioner was abolished.
proposals.after: The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was restored; the vice censor-in-chief of the detached Censorate at the eastern capital held the post concurrently; it again held Ru Prefecture; the Shanxi West defense and observation commissioner was abolished.

proposals.before: Before long, the five prefectures and Jin Prefecture were abolished; he became military commissioner of the Capital Region Shang Prefecture.
proposals.after: Before long, the five prefectures and Jin Prefecture were removed from his charge; the post became military commissioner of the Capital Region Shang Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 罷 here means those jurisdictions were dropped from the commission, not that the prefectures themselves were abolished.

proposals.before: A Shanxi West chief defense commissioner was appointed and soon raised to military commissioner.
proposals.after: A Shaanxi chief defense commissioner was appointed and soon raised to military commissioner.
proposals.reason: 陝西 in this Tang table is the region west of Shan, not Shanxi (山西); Shaanxi matches the toponym used later as Shan–Guo.

proposals.before: In 882, the second year of Zhonghe, the Wei–Bei military commissioner was granted the honorific name Baoda Army circuit, gained Zhai Prefecture, and the Case Army circuit was established at Yan Prefecture.
proposals.after: In 882, the second year of Zhonghe, the Wei–Bei military commissioner was granted the honorific name Baoda Army circuit, gained Zhai Prefecture, and the Baosai Army circuit was established at Yan Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 保塞軍 is the Baosai Army circuit; 'Case Army' is a mistranslation of 塞, not a personal or institutional name in the source.
